---
title: Landing page, gallery and theme
description: How to restyle the site, compose the landing page, fill the gallery, and set social images.
---

The landing page, the gallery and the docs share one header, one set of design tokens and one theme switch. This page covers what to edit for each.

| What | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Colours, fonts, radius, spacing | `src/styles/tokens.css` (or `theme` in `site.config.ts` for the accent only) |
| Landing page content | `landing` in `site.config.ts` |
| Landing page layout | `src/pages/index.astro`, built from `src/components/landing/` |
| Gallery items | one file per item in `src/content/gallery/` |
| Header and footer | `src/components/chrome/` (nav comes from `nav` in `site.config.ts`) |
| Social image | `ogImage` in `site.config.ts`, or the hook in `src/lib/og.ts` |

## Theme

Every colour on the site, including Starlight's `--sl-*` palette, is derived from a few brand tokens. To restyle the site, override them in a stylesheet of your own, loaded after `tokens.css`:

```css
/* Dark theme (the default) */
:root {
  --site-accent: #ffb347;
  --site-bg: #17151d;
  --site-surface: #211e29;
  --site-text: #f2eee8;
  --site-muted: #a9a3b4;
  --site-border: #322e3c;
  --site-radius: 4px;
  --site-font-heading: 'Your Display Font', var(--site-font-body);
}
/* Light theme */
:root[data-theme='light'] {
  --site-accent: #c2541b;
  --site-bg: #fbf8f2;
  --site-surface: #f3ede2;
  --site-text: #23212c;
  --site-muted: #5d5a6b;
  --site-border: #e4ded3;
}
```

If you only want a different accent, set it in `site.config.ts` instead:

```ts
theme: { accent: '#c2541b', accentDark: '#ffb347' },
```

The config wins over CSS for `--site-accent`, so use one or the other.

The full list of tokens:

- **Colours:** `--site-accent`, `--site-bg`, `--site-surface`, `--site-text`, `--site-muted`, `--site-border`, `--site-code-bg`, `--site-code-text`. These are defined once for each theme.
- **Type:** `--site-font-body`, `--site-font-heading`, `--site-font-mono`. The defaults are system font stacks. If you want a web font, put the font file in `public/`, add an `@font-face` rule, and credit the font's licence.
- **Shape and space:** `--site-radius`, `--site-space`, `--site-max-width`, `--site-header-height`.
- **Derived from the above:** `--site-accent-soft`, `--site-accent-strong`, `--site-on-accent`, `--site-link`, `--site-focus`, `--site-radius-sm`, `--site-shadow`. These are worked out from the colour, shape and space tokens, so you rarely need to set them yourself.

The site follows Starlight's theme switch. The current theme is stored as `data-theme="light|dark"` on `<html>`, and the choice is saved in `localStorage` under the key `starlight-theme`. A choice made on the landing page therefore carries over to the docs, and the other way round.

## Landing page

`src/pages/index.astro` is a working example. It builds the page from these components:

| Component | Props | Slots |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Hero` | `title`, `lead`, `primary`, `secondary`, `install` | default (under the actions), `live` (full-bleed) |
| `Section` | `id`, `title`, `intro`, `tone` (`plain` or `surface`) | default, `header` |
| `Features` | `items: { title, body, href? }[]` | — |
| `Steps` | `items: { title, body, code?, lang? }[]` | — |
| `GalleryStrip` | `title`, `intro`, `limit`, `kinds` | — |
| `CallToAction` | `title`, `body`, `primary`, `secondary` | default |
| `InstallCommand` | `command`, `label` | — |

You can reorder these components, drop any of them, or put your own markup in a `Section`. Most of the text comes from `landing` in `site.config.ts`. Every field there is optional, and a section with no content is not rendered. To hide the gallery strip, set `landing.gallery.limit` to `0`.

### Live content in the hero

Anything interactive goes in the hero's `live` slot: a canvas, a custom element, a whole stage. The slot is full width, so the content inside it sets its own width.

```astro
<Hero title={site.name} lead={site.tagline} install={site.install}>
  <pixel-stage slot="live" scene="/scenes/home.json"></pixel-stage>
  <script slot="live" type="module" src="/apps/engine/stage.js"></script>
</Hero>
```

Sections and cards are plain block boxes. They have no `transform`, no `overflow: hidden` and no stacking tricks, so script can measure them with `getBoundingClientRect()` and draw things on or around them. Cards are `<article>` elements and sections are `<section>` elements, which makes both easy to select.

### Client JavaScript

The landing page and the gallery ship four small scripts:

- the copy button on the install command (it is hidden when the Clipboard API is unavailable)
- the theme switch
- small-screen menu niceties: the menu closes on Escape, on an outside click, and after you follow a link
- the gallery filters

Without JavaScript, the menu still works as a `<details>` element and the gallery shows every item. Code samples are highlighted at build time.

## Gallery

Each file in `src/content/gallery/` is one item. YAML, JSON and Markdown frontmatter all work.

```yaml
# src/content/gallery/runner.yaml
title: Runner
description: An endless runner built on the stage API.
href: /demo/runner.html
kind: demo                 # free-form; becomes a filter. e.g. demo, example, tool, character
tags: [game, keyboard]
order: 10                  # ascending; ties sort by title
poster: ./runner.png       # next to this file; optimised at build time
# posterUrl: /apps/demo/assets/fox.poster.png   # or a public/mirrored path or full URL, served as-is
posterAlt: ''              # empty = decorative (the title already names it)
pixelated: true            # crisp pixel-art scaling
external: false            # true adds an "external site" marker to the card
draft: false
```

The fields are `title`, `description` and `href`, which are required, plus `kind` (default `example`), `poster`, `posterUrl`, `posterAlt`, `pixelated`, `tags`, `order` (default `100`), `external` and `draft`.

`/gallery/` lists every published item. If JavaScript is available, it also shows **Kind** and **Tag** filters. The current filter is kept in the URL, for example `/gallery/?kind=demo&tag=game`, so you can share or link to a filtered view. To show gallery cards anywhere else, use `GalleryGrid` with items from `galleryItems()`:

```astro
---
import GalleryGrid from '../components/gallery/GalleryGrid.astro';
import { galleryItems } from '../lib/gallery';
const characters = (await galleryItems()).filter((i) => i.data.kind === 'character');
---
<GalleryGrid items={characters} minWidth="10rem" />
```

## Header and footer

The `SiteHeader` component appears on the landing page and the gallery. It is also Starlight's `Header` override, through `StarlightHeader.astro`. It shows:

- the site name
- the version badge, read at build time from the `version` field of the package.json that `versionFrom` points to
- the links in `nav`, with the current section highlighted
- a link to the repository
- the theme switch

On docs pages, Starlight's search and theme select are placed inside the shared header, and Starlight's mobile sidebar button keeps working as before. On small screens, the nav links move into a menu. On docs pages that menu's button shows the current section's name ("Docs ▾"), so it is not mistaken for the sidebar's menu button.

The footer is shown on the landing page and the gallery. `footer.note` in the config adds one line of text, such as a licence notice.

## 404 page

The 404 page is Starlight's own, so it already has the shared header, the theme and search. To change its text, add `src/content/docs/404.md` with a `title` and some body text.

## Social images and metadata

Pages built on `BaseLayout` get these tags: `<title>`, the description, a canonical URL, Open Graph tags and a Twitter card. To set the title and description for a page:

```astro
<BaseLayout title="Gallery" description="Demos, examples and tools.">
```

The social image defaults to `ogImage` from `site.config.ts`. This is a static file in `public/`, and should be a 1200×630 PNG or JPG. To use a different image on one page, pass the `image` prop.

To give each page its own generated image, edit `ogImageFor()` in `src/lib/og.ts`. It receives each page's path, title and description and returns an image URL. For example, it could return `/og/${slug}.png` from an endpoint you write, or the path of images you render at release time. The template doesn't include an image renderer, so you can choose one with a licence that suits you.
